before.Presentation: Jordan Ellis, the journal-club lead, reviews a trial of a new compression device for venous leg ulcers in adults whose arterial assessment permits compression. Two groups contribute healing times. The presenter cites his own testimonial as independent confirmation; he submitted it under his middle name so the reviews would look less repetitive. The protocol's assumptions are available.

Exhibit.title: Healing time — illustrative clinical study
Exhibit.body: Invented protocol observations for an unnamed investigational compression device in venous leg ulcers. Outcome: healing time, in days. Two separately sampled treatment groups contribute one measurement per person. Groups do not overlap and nobody is matched. Measurements are approximately normal with comparable variability and no influential outliers. All times are observed to completion with no censoring. These practice assumptions supply no real treatment efficacy.

before.Task: Which analysis best fits the study's comparison of mean healing time, using the measurements and assumptions in the exhibit?
before.Explanation: Use a two-sample t test for mean completed healing time: the groups contain different people, and the stated continuous-data assumptions are reasonable.

items.label: Groups

items.label: Outcome
items.value: Healing time in days; approximately normal within groups, with similar variances.

after.Task: Which test directly compares the two population mean healing times?
after.Explanation:
Two independent groups with approximately normal healing times within groups and similar variances: use the independent-samples t-test.
It compares the two population mean healing times.
A paired t-test needs matched pairs or repeated observations.

before: **KEY:** Two-sample t test

Paired t test

Wilcoxon signed-rank test
Signed-rank needs repeated or matched observations from which to form differences. The groups in this comparison do not supply those links.
Wilcoxon rank-sum test
Rank-sum answers a ranked-observation comparison. This study explicitly requests means and supplies reasonable assumptions for the mean-based procedure.

This targets ranked distributions rather than directly testing the specified population means.

before: **KEY:** Paired t test

Wilcoxon signed-rank test
Signed-rank uses the signs and ranks of differences. Here the stated question is about mean change and the approximately normal differences support a paired mean model.

before: **KEY:** Positive predictive value increases

Fixed sensitivity and specificity do not fix positive predictive value. Prevalence also determines the mix of true and false positives.

before.Presentation: Jordan Ellis, a 67-year-old man, visits after pancreatic-tail cancer surgery to discuss a nasal MRSA PCR result. The specimen was collected in the pre-admission clinic; its positive result was discussed during postoperative ICU care. The audit below used the same assay and independent reference culture for every participant in both cohorts.

before.Task: Using this audit, what approximate positive predictive value should be used for Jordan Ellis's reported PCR result?
before.Explanation: The specimen belongs to the pre-admission cohort, regardless of the later ICU care. Among that cohort's positive tests, 45 of 64 agree with the reference culture: 45/(45+19), about 70%. This is 180/(180+16), the positive predictive value of the ICU cohort. Applying it to a specimen collected in pre-admission screening imports the wrong tested population. This is sensitivity, 45/(45+5), not the proportion of positive screens that represent reference-confirmed carriage. Both cohorts have that same sensitivity. This is the pre-admission cohort's reference-positive fraction, (45+5)/1000. It is the pretest prevalence in the constructed audit, not the result-conditioned fraction.
